title: The Hunger Games Tops China's Weekend Box Office as Market Remains Sluggish
excerpt:
Sunrise on the Reaping opens at No. 1 in China with $5.9 million over three days.
The wider market remains weak, with year-to-date revenue nearly 30% below 2025.
body_md:
Lionsgate's The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened at the top of mainland China's box office over the November 20–22, 2026 weekend. According to figures from Artisan Gateway, the dystopian prequel earned RMB39.3 million, approximately $5.9 million, across its first three days. It led the rankings despite a subdued theatrical market that generated only $16 million in total weekend revenue.

The opening illustrates an important distinction between winning the weekend and delivering a blockbuster-sized result. Sunrise on the Reaping finished ahead of its competitors, but China's late-autumn box office remains unusually soft. Year-to-date theatrical revenue has reached roughly $4.8 billion, 29.9% below the corresponding period in 2025. That broader weakness provides essential context for evaluating the new film's performance.

Second place went to New Classics Pictures' crime drama Traces of Justice, which added $2.1 million during its eighth weekend. Its cumulative box office now stands at $113.6 million since opening on October 1. Directed by Chen Sicheng and starring Zhang Yi, Ma Li and Chen Minghao, the film follows a public-security investigator through major criminal cases inspired by real events. Its continued presence near the top of the chart demonstrates the staying power of established local releases.

The latest Resident Evil horror reboot ranked third, earning $1.7 million in its seventh weekend. The Constantin Film and Sony Pictures production has now accumulated $83 million in China since its October 5 debut. Its sustained theatrical run suggests that recognizable genre properties continue to attract audiences even when the overall market is relatively quiet.

A new local suspense release, Love Test, entered in fourth place with $1.1 million over two days following its November 21 launch. Directed by Hou Xiaoyao, the film adapts the 2011 Colombian-Spanish thriller The Hidden Face. Its story concerns a concert pianist whose girlfriend pretends to disappear to test his loyalty. When another woman enters his life and moves into his mountain home, the situation develops into an unsettling mystery.

The domestic body-swap comedy Mr. & Mrs. Pardon completed the top five with another $900,000 in its eighth weekend. Its cumulative earnings have climbed to $65.5 million since October 1. Directed by Shen Chunyang, the comedy follows a middle-aged married couple whose unexpected exchange of bodies forces them to reconsider their relationship and everyday conflicts. Its continued ticket sales underline the importance of domestic productions to the market's overall performance.

For The Hunger Games franchise, first place is a welcome international result, but the numbers should not be mistaken for evidence that the Chinese box office has recovered. The film's staying power will become clearer over subsequent weekends, particularly as new releases arrive and compete for a limited pool of ticket buyers. The larger industry question is whether upcoming films can reverse the substantial year-on-year decline.
